title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-19
content:
Security Engineering Sync — 2026-03-19
Attendees: Aisha Patel (owner), Marco Chen, Lena Ortiz, Diego Ramos, Priya Nair (SRE), Viktor Ivanov (Infra)
Note: quick standup-style sync focused on active vuln triage, secrets findings, and follow-ups from last week's private deployment threat model session.

Agenda:
- Quick status updates
- Vulnerability triage: dependency CVE and rollout plan
- Secrets scanning: false positives and remediation cadence
- Threat modeling follow-up: Private KMS integration for Private deployments
- Action items and owners

1) Status updates
- Aisha: led initial triage of SEC-342 (high severity dependency vuln). Working with infra to validate reproducibility and scope.
- Marco: ran incremental secrets scans across private-deploy repo; higher FP rate on build artifacts.
- Lena: compiled preliminary threat model notes for Private KMS integration and shared with team (Confluence link in artifacts).
- Diego: coordinated with Product for timeline constraints on Dedicated vs Private rollout windows.

2) Vulnerability triage (SEC-342)
Summary: New high-severity CVE flagged in internal dependency chain (libfoo 2.4.1 -> transitive libbar <=1.8). Affects components in Dedicated and Private build images.
Investigation notes:
- Repro: Marco reproduced local exploit against a containerized dev image using known PoC.
- Scope: only services that ship legacy model loader binary with libfoo are affected (hosted API instances running older image tags unaffected).
- Exploitability: requires authenticated internal caller in worst case, but we treat as high due to potential lateral movement.
Mitigation options considered:
- Patch libfoo to 2.5.0 in affected images and rebuild CI images (recommended).
- Apply temporary WAF rule to block crafted requests where feasible (short-term).
- Roll forward to new image and force a rolling redeploy on Dedicated pools.
Decisions & next steps:
- Owner: Aisha to open a repair PR that bumps libfoo -> 2.5.0 and triggers canary CI. Target: PR by EOD 2026-03-19.
- Owner: Viktor to prepare a Dedicated pool canary redeploy plan and schedule for 2026-03-20 morning with fallbacks.
- Owner: Diego to draft customer communication template for enterprise customers with Dedicated capacity (if redeploy impacts throughput).
- Linked ticket: SEC-342 (see artifacts).

3) Secrets scanning and noise reduction
Current state:
- Recent scan of private-deploy repo flagged ~28 secrets. After triage: 18 are FP (build keys, test tokens), 6 are rotated secrets that require revocation, 4 are valid and need immediate rotation.
Actions:
- Marco to push an updated .gitignore and scanning rule exclusions for build artifact paths by 2026-03-20 to reduce recurring FPs.
- Lena to run a focused hunt for the 4 valid secrets and coordinate with SRE/Priya to rotate and verify revocation. Target rotation complete by 2026-03-22.
- All teams reminded to avoid checking generated artifacts into repo; add pre-commit hook enforcement in infra repo (Diego owner).

Notes on tooling:
- Current scanner version is at 3.1.0; next release includes improved entropy heuristics. We'll test in staging once Marco's rule adjustments land.

4) Threat modeling follow-up: Private KMS integration
Recap from last week:
- Goal: support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) for Private deployments while preserving auditability and minimizing surface area for key exposure.
Open questions discussed:
- Key lifecycle management: who rotates, where are keys stored, and how do we ensure zero-knowledge?
- Agent vs. sidecar model: should the KMS client live in a sidecar process or be integrated in the runtime agent?
- Network flow: which egress rules are required for KMS endpoints from air-gapped/private networks?
Decisions & actions:
- Short-term: adopt sidecar model for KMS client in Private (reduces runtime footprint and isolation). Owner: Lena.
- Design doc: Lena to publish an updated threat model with sequence diagrams and attack surface matrix by 2026-03-24. Linked Confluence page included.
- Proof-of-concept: Viktor + Priya to spin up a testbed (VPC private subnet) that uses an external KMS endpoint via restricted NAT for functional testing. Target: 2026-04-02.
- MUST: document explicit fail-closed behavior if KMS is unreachable for critical operations (no silent downgrade to plaintext keys). Owner: Aisha to add to design doc.

5) Operational notes & monitoring
- Add a dashboard panel for post-deploy vulnerability scan results per image tag (SRE/Observability action). Priya to scope with observability team.
- Add alerting for secret scan trend spikes (>10 new unique findings/day). Marco/Diego to add rule.

6) Action items summary (owners and due dates)
- Aisha: Open patch PR for libfoo -> 2.5.0 and add canary CI job. Due: 2026-03-19.
- Viktor: Canary redeploy plan for Dedicated pools. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Diego: Customer communication draft + pre-commit hook rollout in infra repo. Draft due: 2026-03-20.
- Marco: Update scanner exclusions and reduce FP noise; add alert rule for secret spike. Due: 2026-03-20.
- Lena: Publish updated Private KMS threat model with diagrams. Due: 2026-03-24.
- Priya: Scope dashboard/alert with Observability team for vuln/secret metrics. Due: 2026-03-26.

Parking lot / Questions for execs:
- For Dedicated redeploys that might impact capacity for enterprise customers, do we need a formal maintenance window policy? (Diego to raise with Product Ops).
- For BYO-KMS, legal wants clarity on key custody statement in contract templates. Follow up with Legal.

Next sync: 2026-03-23 10:00 PT (standup format).

Misc notes / links:
- Related tickets: SEC-342 (dependency patch), SEC-350 (secrets rotation automation).
- Confluence: Private KMS threat model draft (see linked artifacts).

End of notes.
